tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

1: /**
2:  * This is the internal implementation of quantiles: when you know
3:  * that the order is sorted, you don't need to re-sort it, and the computations
4:  * are faster.
5:  *
6:  * This implements the linear interpolation method (type=7 in R/numpy),
7:  * which is the default in numpy.percentile and R's quantile.
8:  *
9:  * @param {Array<number>} x sample of one or more data points
10:  * @param {number} p desired quantile: a number between 0 to 1, inclusive
11:  * @returns {number} quantile value
12:  * @throws {Error} if p ix outside of the range from 0 to 1
13:  * @throws {Error} if x is empty
14:  * @example
15:  * quantileSorted([3, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9, 10, 13, 15, 16, 20], 0.5); // => 9
16:  */
17: function quantileSorted(x, p) {
18:     // Use (n-1) * p for index, matching numpy's linear method (type=7)
19:     const idx = (x.length - 1) * p;
20:     if (x.length === 0) {
21:         throw new Error("quantile requires at least one data point.");
22:     }
23:     else if (p < 0 || p > 1) {
24:         throw new Error("quantiles must be between 0 and 1");
25:     }
26:     else if (p === 1) {
27:         // If p is 1, directly return the last element
28:         return x[x.length - 1];
29:     }
30:     else if (p === 0) {
31:         // If p is 0, directly return the first element
32:         return x[0];
33:     }
34:     else if (idx % 1 !== 0) {
35:         // If idx is not integer, interpolate linearly between floor and ceil
36:         const lower = Math.floor(idx);
37:         const upper = Math.ceil(idx);
38:         const fraction = idx - lower;
39:         return x[lower] + fraction * (x[upper] - x[lower]);
40:     }
41:     else {
42:         // If idx is integer, type=7 returns the value at that index
43:         return x[idx];
44:     }
45: }

1: /**
2:  * Rearrange items in `arr` so that all items in `[left, k]` range are the smallest.
3:  * The `k`-th element will have the `(k - left + 1)`-th smallest value in `[left, right]`.
4:  *
5:  * Implements Floyd-Rivest selection algorithm https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd-Rivest_algorithm
6:  *
7:  * @param {Array<number>} arr input array
8:  * @param {number} k pivot index
9:  * @param {number} [left] left index
10:  * @param {number} [right] right index
11:  * @returns {void} mutates input array
12:  * @example
13:  * var arr = [65, 28, 59, 33, 21, 56, 22, 95, 50, 12, 90, 53, 28, 77, 39];
14:  * quickselect(arr, 8);
15:  * // = [39, 28, 28, 33, 21, 12, 22, 50, 53, 56, 59, 65, 90, 77, 95]
16:  */
17: function quickselect(arr, k, left, right) {
18:     left = left || 0;
19:     right = right || arr.length - 1;
20:     while (right > left) {
21:         // 600 and 0.5 are arbitrary constants chosen in the original paper to minimize execution time
22:         if (right - left > 600) {
23:             const n = right - left + 1;
24:             const m = k - left + 1;
25:             const z = Math.log(n);
26:             const s = 0.5 * Math.exp((2 * z) / 3);
27:             let sd = 0.5 * Math.sqrt((z * s * (n - s)) / n);
28:             if (m - n / 2 < 0)
29:                 sd *= -1;
30:             const newLeft = Math.max(left, Math.floor(k - (m * s) / n + sd));
31:             const newRight = Math.min(right, Math.floor(k + ((n - m) * s) / n + sd));
32:             quickselect(arr, k, newLeft, newRight);
33:         }
34:         const t = arr[k];
35:         let i = left;
36:         let j = right;
37:         swap(arr, left, k);
38:         if (arr[right] > t)
39:             swap(arr, left, right);
40:         while (i < j) {
41:             swap(arr, i, j);
42:             i++;
43:             j--;
44:             while (arr[i] < t)
45:                 i++;
46:             while (arr[j] > t)
47:                 j--;
48:         }
49:         if (arr[left] === t)
50:             swap(arr, left, j);
51:         else {
52:             j++;
53:             swap(arr, j, right);
54:         }
55:         if (j <= k)
56:             left = j + 1;
57:         if (k <= j)
58:             right = j - 1;
59:     }
60: }
61: function swap(arr, i, j) {
62:     const tmp = arr[i];
63:     arr[i] = arr[j];
64:     arr[j] = tmp;
65: }
66: export default quickselect;

/**
 * @name lightFormat
 * @category Common Helpers
 * @summary Format the date.
 *
 * @description
 * Return the formatted date string in the given format. Unlike `format`,
 * `lightFormat` doesn't use locales and outputs date using the most popular tokens.
 *
 * > ⚠️ Please note that the `lightFormat` tokens differ from Moment.js and other libraries.
 * > See: https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns/blob/master/docs/unicodeTokens.md
 *
 * The characters wrapped between two single quotes characters (') are escaped.
 * Two single quotes in a row, whether inside or outside a quoted sequence, represent a 'real' single quote.
 *
 * Format of the string is based on Unicode Technical Standard #35:
 * https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/tr35-dates.html#Date_Field_Symbol_Table
 *
 * Accepted patterns:

1	/**
     2	 * The `expect` a synthesized environment's hidden cases run under: a vitest
     3	 * matcher subset small enough to ship without a test runner, so a case runs
     4	 * under plain `node` with nothing installed. The repository factory
     5	 * (`synthesize-repository-tasks.ts`) inlines this file's text verbatim ahead
     6	 * of each case; the public factory (`synthesize-public-tasks.ts`) writes it
     7	 * into each child's workspace as `test/expect-shim.mjs`, immutable, and each
     8	 * case imports it. Both factories admit a spec block only when every matcher
     9	 * it uses is one of these, so a case never reaches a matcher this shim lacks.
    10	 *
    11	 * A failed assertion throws {@link AssertionError}, which an ESM program
    12	 * leaves uncaught: node prints the message and exits non-zero, which is the
    13	 * case's verdict. Semantics follow vitest's for the subset: `toEqual` ignores
    14	 * `undefined`-valued properties and prototypes, `toStrictEqual` checks both,
    15	 * `toMatchObject` requires every expected property recursively and nothing
    16	 * more, `toContain` uses SameValueZero on arrays and substring on strings,
    17	 * `toContainEqual` structural equality on any element, `toBeCloseTo` the
    18	 * vitest bound of half a unit in the last requested decimal, `toHaveProperty`
    19	 * a dotted or array key path with an optional structural value, and `toThrow`
    20	 * (alias `toThrowError`) accepts no argument, a message substring, a RegExp
    21	 * over the message, an Error whose message must match exactly, or an Error
    22	 * class the thrown value must be an instance of;
    23	 * `toThrowErrorMatchingInlineSnapshot` compares the thrown error against
    24	 * vitest's `[Name: message]` rendering. `expectTypeOf` and `assertType` are
    25	 * the runtime no-ops vitest also ships, so a block that checks types beside
    26	 * values runs unchanged.
    27	 */
    28	
    29	/** A failed matcher, carrying the message a case reports on stderr. */
    30	export class AssertionError extends Error {
    31	  /** @param message - what was expected and what was found. */
    32	  constructor(message) {
    33	    super(message)
    34	    this.name = 'AssertionError'
    35	  }
    36	}
    37	
    38	/** A readable rendering of one value for an assertion message. */
    39	function format(value) {
    40	  if (value === undefined) return 'undefined'
    41	  if (typeof value === 'string') return JSON.stringify(value)
    42	  if (typeof value === 'bigint') return `${value}n`
    43	  if (typeof value === 'function') return `[Function ${value.name || 'anonymous'}]`
    44	  if (typeof value === 'symbol') return value.toString()
    45	  if (value instanceof Error) return `${value.name}(${JSON.stringify(value.message)})`
    46	  if (value instanceof RegExp) return value.toString()
    47	  try {
    48	    return JSON.stringify(value, (_key, inner) => (typeof inner === 'bigint' ? `${inner}n` : inner === undefined ? 'undefined' : inner)) ?? String(value)
    49	  } catch {
    50	    // JSON.stringify throws on a cycle; the message then names the value's type instead of its contents.
    51	    return Object.prototype.toString.call(value)
    52	  }
    53	}
    54	
    55	/** Own enumerable string keys, dropping the `undefined`-valued ones unless `strict`. */
    56	function keysOf(value, strict) {
    57	  return Object.keys(value).filter(key => strict || value[key] !== undefined)
    58	}
    59	
    60	/**
    61	 * Structural equality: `Object.is` on primitives, then arrays, typed arrays,
    62	 * `Date`, `RegExp`, `Error`, `Map`, `Set`, and plain objects by content. A
    63	 * pair already being compared higher in the recursion counts as equal, so a
    64	 * cycle terminates.
    65	 */
    66	function equals(left, right, strict, seen = []) {
    67	  if (Object.is(left, right)) return true
    68	  if (typeof left !== 'object' || typeof right !== 'object' || left === null || right === null) return false
    69	  if (seen.some(([a, b]) => a === left && b === right)) return true
    70	  const pairs = [...seen, [left, right]]
    71	  if (strict && Object.getPrototypeOf(left) !== Object.getPrototypeOf(right)) return false
    72	  if (left instanceof Date || right instanceof Date) return left instanceof Date && right instanceof Date && left.getTime() === right.getTime()
    73	  if (left instanceof RegExp || right instanceof RegExp) return left instanceof RegExp && right instanceof RegExp && left.source === right.source && left.flags === right.flags
    74	  if (left instanceof Error || right instanceof Error) {
    75	    return left instanceof Error && right instanceof Error && left.name === right.name && left.message === right.message
    76	  }
    77	  if (ArrayBuffer.isView(left) || ArrayBuffer.isView(right)) {
    78	    if (!ArrayBuffer.isView(left) || !ArrayBuffer.isView(right) || left.length !== right.length) return false
    79	    for (let index = 0; index < left.length; index += 1) if (left[index] !== right[index]) return false
    80	    return true
    81	  }
    82	  if (Array.isArray(left) || Array.isArray(right)) {
    83	    if (!Array.isArray(left) || !Array.isArray(right) || left.length !== right.length) return false
    84	    return left.every((item, index) => equals(item, right[index], strict, pairs))
    85	  }
    86	  if (left instanceof Map || right instanceof Map) {
    87	    if (!(left instanceof Map) || !(right instanceof Map) || left.size !== right.size) return false
    88	    for (const [key, value] of left) {
    89	      const match = [...right].find(([otherKey]) => equals(key, otherKey, strict, pairs))
    90	      if (match === undefined || !equals(value, match[1], strict, pairs)) return false
    91	    }
    92	    return true
    93	  }
    94	  if (left instanceof Set || right instanceof Set) {
    95	    if (!(left instanceof Set) || !(right instanceof Set) || left.size !== right.size) return false
    96	    for (const item of left) if (![...right].some(other => equals(item, other, strict, pairs))) return false
    97	    return true
    98	  }
    99	  const leftKeys = keysOf(left, strict)
   100	  const rightKeys = keysOf(right, strict)
   101	  if (leftKeys.length !== rightKeys.length) return false
   102	  return leftKeys.every(key => rightKeys.includes(key) && equals(left[key], right[key], strict, pairs))
   103	}
   104	
   105	/** The message text of a thrown value, whatever its type. */
   106	function thrownMessage(thrown) {
   107	  return thrown instanceof Error ? thrown.message : String(thrown)
   108	}
   109	
   110	/** Whether `thrown` satisfies `expected` under `toThrow`'s argument forms. */
   111	function throwMatches(thrown, expected) {
   112	  if (expected === undefined) return true
   113	  if (typeof expected === 'string') return thrownMessage(thrown).includes(expected)
   114	  if (expected instanceof RegExp) return expected.test(thrownMessage(thrown))
   115	  if (expected instanceof Error) return thrownMessage(thrown) === expected.message
   116	  if (typeof expected === 'function') return thrown instanceof expected
   117	  throw new TypeError(`toThrow does not accept ${format(expected)}`)
   118	}
   119	
   120	/** vitest's inline-snapshot rendering of a thrown value: `[Name: message]` for an Error, the quoted string otherwise. */
   121	function snapshotOf(thrown) {
   122	  return thrown instanceof Error ? `[${thrown.name}: ${thrown.message}]` : JSON.stringify(String(thrown))
   123	}
   124	
   125	/** Whether `actual` carries every property of `expected`, recursively, with anything else allowed beside them. */
   126	function matchesObject(actual, expected, seen = []) {
   127	  if (typeof expected !== 'object' || expected === null || typeof actual !== 'object' || actual === null) return equals(actual, expected, false)
   128	  if (seen.some(([a, b]) => a === actual && b === expected)) return true
   129	  const pairs = [...seen, [actual, expected]]
   130	  if (Array.isArray(expected)) {
   131	    return Array.isArray(actual) && actual.length === expected.length && expected.every((item, index) => matchesObject(actual[index], item, pairs))
   132	  }
   133	  if (expected instanceof Date || expected instanceof RegExp || expected instanceof Error || expected instanceof Map || expected instanceof Set) {
   134	    return equals(actual, expected, false)
   135	  }
   136	  return Object.keys(expected).every(key => key in actual && matchesObject(actual[key], expected[key], pairs))
   137	}
   138	
   139	/** The segments of a `toHaveProperty` key path: an array as given, a string split on dots. */
   140	function keyPath(path) {
   141	  return Array.isArray(path) ? path : String(path).split('.')
   142	}
   143	
   144	/**
   145	 * The matcher set over one value, negated or not. Each matcher decides a pass
   146	 * and a description; `verdict` throws when the pass disagrees with the
   147	 * negation, so `not` costs one flag rather than a second set of matchers.
   148	 */
   149	function matchers(actual, negated) {
   150	  const verdict = (pass, description) => {
   151	    if (pass !== negated) return
   152	    throw new AssertionError(`expected ${format(actual)} ${negated ? 'not ' : ''}${description}`)
   153	  }
   154	  const lengthOf = () => (actual !== null && actual !== undefined && typeof actual.length === 'number' ? actual.length : undefined)
   155	  const throws = () => {
   156	    if (typeof actual !== 'function') throw new TypeError(`toThrow needs a function, got ${format(actual)}`)
   157	    try {
   158	      actual()
   159	    } catch (thrown) {
   160	      return { thrown }
   161	    }
   162	    return undefined
   163	  }
   164	  const toThrow = (expected) => {
   165	    const outcome = throws()
   166	    const description = expected === undefined ? 'to throw' : `to throw ${format(expected)}`
   167	    verdict(outcome !== undefined && throwMatches(outcome.thrown, expected), outcome === undefined ? description : `${description}, got ${format(outcome.thrown)}`)
   168	  }
   169	  const iterableHas = predicate => actual !== null && actual !== undefined && typeof actual[Symbol.iterator] === 'function' && Array.from(actual).some(predicate)
   170	  return {
   171	    toBe: expected => verdict(Object.is(actual, expected), `to be ${format(expected)}`),
   172	    toEqual: expected => verdict(equals(actual, expected, false), `to equal ${format(expected)}`),
   173	    toStrictEqual: expected => verdict(equals(actual, expected, true), `to strictly equal ${format(expected)}`),
   174	    toMatchObject: expected => verdict(matchesObject(actual, expected), `to match object ${format(expected)}`),
   175	    toBeUndefined: () => verdict(actual === undefined, 'to be undefined'),
   176	    toBeDefined: () => verdict(actual !== undefined, 'to be defined'),
   177	    toBeNull: () => verdict(actual === null, 'to be null'),
   178	    toBeNaN: () => verdict(Number.isNaN(actual), 'to be NaN'),
   179	    toBeTruthy: () => verdict(Boolean(actual), 'to be truthy'),
   180	    toBeFalsy: () => verdict(!actual, 'to be falsy'),
   181	    toBeTypeOf: expected => verdict(typeof actual === expected, `to be of type ${format(expected)}`),
   182	    toBeInstanceOf: expected => verdict(actual instanceof expected, `to be an instance of ${format(expected)}`),
   183	    toHaveLength: expected => verdict(lengthOf() === expected, `to have length ${format(expected)}`),
   184	    toHaveProperty: (path, ...value) => {
   185	      let cursor = actual
   186	      let present = true
   187	      for (const key of keyPath(path)) {
   188	        if (cursor === null || cursor === undefined || !(key in Object(cursor))) {
   189	          present = false
   190	          break
   191	        }
   192	        cursor = cursor[key]
   193	      }
   194	      const holds = present && (value.length === 0 || equals(cursor, value[0], false))
   195	      verdict(holds, `to have property ${format(path)}${value.length === 0 ? '' : ` equal to ${format(value[0])}`}`)
   196	    },
   197	    toContain: (expected) => {
   198	      const holds = typeof actual === 'string' ? actual.includes(expected) : iterableHas(item => Object.is(item, expected) || item === expected)
   199	      verdict(holds, `to contain ${format(expected)}`)
   200	    },
   201	    toContainEqual: expected => verdict(iterableHas(item => equals(item, expected, false)), `to contain an item equal to ${format(expected)}`),
   202	    toThrow,
   203	    toThrowError: toThrow,
   204	    toThrowErrorMatchingInlineSnapshot: (snapshot) => {
   205	      const outcome = throws()
   206	      const rendered = outcome === undefined ? undefined : snapshotOf(outcome.thrown)
   207	      verdict(rendered !== undefined && rendered === String(snapshot).trim(), `to throw an error rendering as ${format(String(snapshot).trim())}${rendered === undefined ? '' : `, got ${format(rendered)}`}`)
   208	    },
   209	    toMatch: (expected) => {
   210	      if (typeof actual !== 'string') throw new TypeError(`toMatch needs a string, got ${format(actual)}`)
   211	      verdict(expected instanceof RegExp ? expected.test(actual) : actual.includes(expected), `to match ${format(expected)}`)
   212	    },
   213	    toBeGreaterThan: expected => verdict(actual > expected, `to be greater than ${format(expected)}`),
   214	    toBeGreaterThanOrEqual: expected => verdict(actual >= expected, `to be at least ${format(expected)}`),
   215	    toBeLessThan: expected => verdict(actual < expected, `to be less than ${format(expected)}`),
   216	    toBeLessThanOrEqual: expected => verdict(actual <= expected, `to be at most ${format(expected)}`),
   217	    toBeCloseTo: (expected, digits = 2) => {
   218	      const holds = actual === Infinity && expected === Infinity || actual === -Infinity && expected === -Infinity
   219	        || Math.abs(expected - actual) < 10 ** -digits / 2
   220	      verdict(holds, `to be close to ${format(expected)} within ${digits} decimal places`)
   221	    },
   222	  }
   223	}
   224	
   225	/**
   226	 * The assertion entry point, as a case program calls it.
   227	 * @param actual - the value under assertion.
   228	 * @returns the matcher subset over `actual`, with `not` negating each matcher.
   229	 */
   230	export function expect(actual) {
   231	  return { ...matchers(actual, false), not: matchers(actual, true) }
   232	}
   233	
   234	/** A callable whose every property is itself, so any chain of type-assertion calls returns without effect. */
   235	const inert = new Proxy(function inert() {}, {
   236	  get: (_target, key) => (key === Symbol.toPrimitive ? () => '' : inert),
   237	  apply: () => inert,
   238	})
   239	
   240	/**
   241	 * vitest's `expectTypeOf`, which asserts nothing at runtime: the type check
   242	 * lives in the compiler, and the JavaScript build of a spec keeps the call.
   243	 * @returns an inert chain accepting any matcher.
   244	 */
   245	export function expectTypeOf() {
   246	  return inert
   247	}
   248	
   249	/**
   250	 * vitest's `assertType`, a runtime no-op that types its argument.
   251	 */
   252	export function assertType() {}

# Implement camelCase from case-anything

`src/core.js` is the JavaScript build of `src/core.ts` from case-anything (https://github.com/mesqueeb/case-anything at commit b0e95907e6a8, MIT licence, whose text is in `LICENSE`). Every export of the module is in place except `camelCase`, whose body currently throws 'not implemented'. Implement only that function's body so that it fulfills its own documentation, which the source carries as follows:

/**
 * # 🐪 camelCase
 *
 * Converts a string to camelCase
 *
 * - First lowercase then all capitalised
 * - _strips away_ special characters by default
 *
 * @example
 *   camelCase('$catDog') === 'catDog'
 *
 * @example
 *   camelCase('$catDog', { keepSpecialCharacters: true }) === '$catDog'
 */
export function camelCase(
  string: string,
  options?: { keepSpecialCharacters?: boolean; keep?: string[] },
): string

Keep the signature exactly as given, and do not edit any other file, export, or function; `README.md` states the types the signature and the documentation name. The other files under `src/` (`src/utils.js`) are the module's own dependencies, unchanged; read them as you need, edit none. Add no dependencies: `package.json` is fixed and `node_modules` must not exist. This task is judged on inputs you do not see: a validator runs the module's own test suite, which this workspace does not contain, against your implementation. `test/expect-shim.mjs` is the assertion library those cases run under; it holds no case and is fixed. Implement the documented contract, including every corner it states, rather than the behaviour a guessed test would pin down.

## Attribution

This task is derived from `src/core.ts` of case-anything (https://github.com/mesqueeb/case-anything) at commit `b0e95907e6a81c0417915db3bd1c910a706fd666`, distributed under the MIT licence (Copyright (c) 2019 Luca Ban - Mesqueeb); the licence text is kept in `LICENSE` and accompanies every copy of this task and anything derived from it.

import { capitaliseWord, magicSplit, splitAndPrefix } from './utils.js'

/**
 * # 🐪 camelCase
 *
 * Converts a string to camelCase
 *
 * - First lowercase then all capitalised
 * - _strips away_ special characters by default
 *
 * @example
 *   camelCase('$catDog') === 'catDog'
 *
 * @example
 *   camelCase('$catDog', { keepSpecialCharacters: true }) === '$catDog'
 */
export function camelCase(
  string: string,
  options?: { keepSpecialCharacters?: boolean; keep?: string[] },
): string {
  return splitAndPrefix(string, options).reduce((result, word, index) => {
    return index === 0 || !(word[0] || '').match(magicSplit)
      ? result + word.toLowerCase()
      : result + capitaliseWord(word)
  }, '')
}

// Latin-1 Supplement
// upper case ranges
// [À-ÖØ-ß]
// lower case ranges
// [à-öø-ÿ]

export const magicSplit =
  /^[a-zà-öø-ÿа-я]+|[A-ZÀ-ÖØ-ßА-Я][a-zà-öø-ÿа-я]+|[a-zà-öø-ÿа-я]+|[0-9]+|[A-ZÀ-ÖØ-ßА-Я]+(?![a-zà-öø-ÿа-я])/g
export const spaceSplit = /\S+/g

/**
 * A string.matchAll function that will return an array of "string parts" and the indexes at which
 * it split each part
 */
export function getPartsAndIndexes(
  string: string,
  splitRegex: RegExp,
): {
  parts: string[]
  prefixes: string[]
} {
  const result = { parts: [] as string[], prefixes: [] as string[] }
  const matches = string.matchAll(splitRegex)

  let lastWordEndIndex = 0
  for (const match of matches) {
    if (typeof match.index !== 'number') continue

    const word = match[0]
    result.parts.push(word)

    const prefix = string.slice(lastWordEndIndex, match.index).trim()
    result.prefixes.push(prefix)

    lastWordEndIndex = match.index + word.length
  }
  const tail = string.slice(lastWordEndIndex).trim()
  if (tail) {
    result.parts.push('')
    result.prefixes.push(tail)
  }

  return result
}

/**
 * A function that splits a string on words and returns an array of words.
 *
 * - It can prefix each word with a given character
 * - It can strip or keep special characters, this affects the logic for adding a prefix as well
 */
export function splitAndPrefix(
  string: string,
  options?: { keepSpecialCharacters?: boolean; keep?: string[]; prefix?: string },
): string[] {
  const { keepSpecialCharacters = false, keep, prefix = '' } = options || {}
  const normalString = string.trim().normalize('NFC')
  const hasSpaces = normalString.includes(' ')
  const split = hasSpaces ? spaceSplit : magicSplit
  const partsAndIndexes = getPartsAndIndexes(normalString, split)

  return partsAndIndexes.parts
    .map((_part, i) => {
      let foundPrefix = partsAndIndexes.prefixes[i] || ''
      let part = _part

      if (keepSpecialCharacters === false) {
        if (keep) {
          part = part
            .normalize('NFD')
            .replace(new RegExp(`[^a-zA-ZØßø0-9${keep.join('')}]`, 'g'), '')
        }
        if (!keep) {
          part = part.normalize('NFD').replace(/[^a-zA-ZØßø0-9]/g, '')
          foundPrefix = ''
        }
      }

      if (keep && foundPrefix) {
        foundPrefix = foundPrefix.replace(new RegExp(`[^${keep.join('')}]`, 'g'), '')
      }

      // the first word doesn't need a prefix, so only return the found prefix
      if (i === 0) {
        // console.log(`foundPrefix → `, foundPrefix)
        return foundPrefix + part
      }

      if (!foundPrefix && !part) return ''

      if (!hasSpaces) {
        // return the found prefix OR fall back to a given prefix
        return (foundPrefix || prefix) + part
      }

      // space based sentence was split on spaces, so only return found prefixes
      if (!foundPrefix && prefix.match(/\s/)) {
        // in this case we have no more found prefix, it was trimmed, but we're looking to add a space
        // so let's return that space
        return ' ' + part
      }
      return (foundPrefix || prefix) + part
    })
    .filter(Boolean)
}

/**
 * Capitalises a single word
 *
 * @returns The word with the first character in uppercase and the rest in lowercase
 */
export function capitaliseWord(string: string): string {
  const match = string.matchAll(magicSplit).next().value
  const firstLetterIndex = match ? match.index : 0
  return (
    string.slice(0, firstLetterIndex + 1).toUpperCase() +
    string.slice(firstLetterIndex + 1).toLowerCase()
  )
}
